title: Query-OOD Escalation: Detecting Memory Poisoning Attacks via Embedding-Space Anomaly Detection

contributions.purpose: Show that AgentPoison's trigger optimization leaves a detectable geometric signature in query embedding space.
contributions.mechanism: Exploit the attack's uniqueness objective, which pushes triggered query embeddings out-of-distribution relative to benign clusters, and detect them with an LDA-based OOD gate.
contributions.evaluation: The detection gate achieves perfect separation (AUROC=1.0) between benign and AgentPoison-triggered queries on ReAct-StrategyQA, with zero false positives at 99% true positive rate.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that AgentPoison's uniqueness objective creates a detectable geometric signature, enabling an OOD detection gate that achieves AUROC=1.0 with zero false positives at 99% true positive rate.

contributions.purpose: Provide a selective defense-routing framework that screens adversarial queries before they reach the agent.
contributions.mechanism: Query-OOD Escalation (QOE) routes queries through the LDA detection gate, escalating detected queries to stronger consensus validation or stripping detected triggers before processing.
contributions.evaluation: QOE achieves 100% adversarial detection while flagging only 7.42% of benign queries.
contributions.source_quote: We propose QOE, a framework for selective defense routing that achieves 100% adversarial detection while flagging only 7.42% of benign queries.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate end-to-end attack mitigation at lower cost than consensus-based defenses.
contributions.mechanism: QOE-Reject drops queries flagged by the detection gate instead of running expensive A-MemGuard-style consensus validation on every query.
contributions.evaluation: QOE-Reject reduces attack success rate by 4.25 percentage points while maintaining benign accuracy, outperforming consensus escalation on benchmarks with low retrieval rates.
contributions.source_quote: We show that QOE-Reject reduces attack success rate by 4.25 percentage points while maintaining benign accuracy, outperforming consensus escalation on benchmarks with low retrieval rates.

contributions.purpose: Establish robustness of the detection approach against adaptive attackers.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate adaptive attackers who reduce trigger uniqueness to evade OOD detection and characterize the resulting evasion-vs-retrieval trade-off.
contributions.evaluation: Detection remains robust; reducing trigger uniqueness to evade detection degrades the attack's retrieval effectiveness, revealing a fundamental trade-off.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate robustness against adaptive attackers who reduce trigger uniqueness, revealing a fundamental trade-off between evasion and retrieval effectiveness.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by exploiting the attacker's optimization objective to detect triggered queries before they reach the defense mechanism, enabling selective escalation.

We apply these techniques to query embeddings, observing that AgentPoison's uniqueness objective inadvertently creates a detectable geometric signature. Unlike prior OOD detection work focused on image classification, we demonstrate that embedding-space anomaly detection can effectively identify adversarial queries in LLM agent systems.
Our work demonstrates that detection-based defenses can effectively complement consensus mechanisms for LLM agent security.

notes: Perfect detection metrics (AUROC=1.0) contrast with a modest end-to-end gain: QOE-Reject reduces attack success rate by only 4.25 percentage points. Defense is specific to AgentPoison's uniqueness objective on one benchmark (ReAct-StrategyQA).
